blocks.arabic_text: رَبَّنَا اٰتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَّفِي الْاٰخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَّقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
blocks.text: "O our Rabb, grant us (all that which is) good in this world, (all that which is) good in the Aakhirah and save us from the punishment of the fire (of Jahannam)." {Surah Baqarah, verse 201}
The man then made the du'aa and was cured.[^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Refuses to Make Du'aa for Hadhrat Basheer bin Khasaasiyah (RA) to Die before him

Hadhrat Basheer bin Khasaasiyah (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to him, "Thank Allaah for bringing you from the Rabee'ah Khath'am tribe and allowing you to accept Islaam at the hands of His Rasool ﷺ." "O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" Hadhrat Basheer (RA) said, "Pray to Allaah to allow me to die before you." Refusing the request, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I shall not make that du'aa for anyone."[^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Begins with Himself when Making Du'aa and Avoids Rhyming

Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) says, "Whenever making du'aa for anyone, Rasulullaah ﷺ always began with (asking for) himself. When speaking of Hadhrat Moosa (AS) one day, Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, 'May Allaah shower His mercy on Moosa (AS). Had he been more patient, he would have seen even stranger things from his companion. However, he said:

blocks.arabic_text: إِنْ سَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ بَعْدَهَا فَلَا تُصٰحِبْنِيْ قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِنْ لَّدُنِّيْ عُذْرًا
blocks.text: "If I question you about anything after this, then you need not remain with me. You have received (enough) excuse from me (to part from me)." {Surah Kahaf, verse 72}[^3]
Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA) also reports that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa, he began with himself.[^4]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once said to Ibn Abu Saa'ib who was the lecturer of Madinah, "Refrain from going out of your way to rhyme your du'aa because I have seen the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) and none of them did this."[^5]
